description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its unified rollouts / A/B testing / model lifecycle system to better support Dedicated (reserved-capacity) customers. The project “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” introduces phased rollout controls for Dedicated GPU capacity pools, allowing operators and customers to safely roll out new model versions, runtime builds, routing policies, or configuration changes via explicit stages with measurable gates.

Goals:
- Provide first-class staged rollout plans for Dedicated pools (per-customer reserved capacity) with stage definitions (e.g., 0%/1%/10%/50%/100% traffic or replica-based partitions) and required gates before promotion.
- Define and enforce gate criteria using objective signals (error rate, p95/p99 latency, saturation/headroom, GPU health, OOM rate, request drop/429, quality regression metrics where applicable).
- Ensure deterministic, auditable, and reversible changes: stage-by-stage promotion, automatic abort/rollback, and clear “freeze/hold” states.
- Integrate into Redwood Console rollout workflows and underlying policy engine / routing layer so staged rollouts apply consistently across regions and failure modes.

Scope:
- Control plane: data model for “DedicatedPoolRolloutPlan”, APIs for create/update/promote/abort, and audit trail entries.
- Routing + data plane: traffic splitting/partitioning by stage for Dedicated pools, safe fallback behavior, and protection against capacity starvation.
- Observability: stage dashboards, standardized SLO gate queries, and alerting for gate failures.
- Console UX/backend: UI representation of stages, promotion buttons, gate evaluation details, and change history.
- Release engineering + QA: end-to-end validation, chaos/failure testing (stuck stage, partial capacity, region impairment), and runbooks.

Non-goals (initial release):
- Fully general “arbitrary experiment platform” for Dedicated beyond rollout safety (A/B experimentation is supported only insofar as it’s used as a gated rollout mechanism).
- Customer-self-serve arbitrary custom metrics for gating (initially Redwood-defined metrics + limited config).

Stakeholders / teams:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Paula Mendes (rollout policy PM).
- Engineering: Ethan Park (Platform Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing), Chloe Martin / Jada Williams (Console Backend), Vikram Singh (Data Plane), Logan Wright (Telemetry).
- Infra/SRE: Irene Choi / Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet), Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (SRE), Allison Grant (Observability standards).
- Release/QA: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng), Leila Farouk (QA automation).
- Security review touchpoints: Kaitlyn Nguyen (authn/authz), audit logging team.

Timeline (proposed):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): requirements, success criteria, and MVP stage model aligned across Product/Dedicated/SRE.
- Phase 1 (3–5 weeks): control plane + routing primitives, behind feature flags; initial “manual gates” (operator-verified).
- Phase 2 (3–4 weeks): automated gate evaluation + Console UI + dashboards/alerts.
- Phase 3 (2–3 weeks): dogfood on internal Dedicated pools, then limited beta with 1–2 design partners; iterate on rollback and edge cases.
- Phase 4: GA launch, docs/runbooks, and post-launch reliability review.

Key deliverables:
- PRD + design spec + ADRs (gate model, traffic splitting approach, audit model).
- Implemented APIs and policy engine rules; Console workflow; stage dashboards; runbooks.
- Validation artifacts: load tests, failure-mode tests, and launch checklist.

Constraints:
- Must not jeopardize Dedicated customer SLOs; gate evaluation must be low-latency and resilient.
- Must coordinate with GPU fleet capacity signals and avoid over-partitioning small pools.
- Must provide clear operational escape hatches (force-promote, force-rollback, hold) with audit logging and RBAC.

files.description: Product Requirements Doc: customer problems (Dedicated pool upgrades), user personas (SRE/operator, customer admin), MVP vs v2 scope, UX requirements in Console, success metrics, rollout plan, and open questions.
End-to-end design spec: architecture overview, APIs, stage model, gate evaluation pipeline, Console UX flows, and integration points with routing/data plane and telemetry.
ADR deciding stage representation (percentage vs replica partitions), how stages map to pool capacity, and trade-offs for small pools and multi-region pools.
ADR defining gate signal sources (metrics/traces), standard thresholds per tier, aggregation windows, and how to handle noisy metrics and missing data.
ADR on rollback behavior: when to auto-abort, how to revert traffic splitting, what to do with in-flight sessions/streams, and required audit events.
Service doc for the new/updated control-plane component managing Dedicated pool rollout plans, including data model, APIs, dependencies, and operational considerations.
Operations runbook: creating a rollout plan, promoting stages, interpreting gate failures, manual override procedures, and emergency rollback steps.
Infra guidelines for partitioning reserved pools during staged rollouts (minimum headroom, per-stage replica sizing, region constraints, and how to avoid fragmentation).
SRE doc mapping gate thresholds to SLOs (latency/error/saturation) and documenting error-budget-based promotion policies.
Audit logging spec for rollout actions (create/update/promote/abort/force-override), RBAC requirements, retention, and example event payloads.
Working notes (PM): MVP scope, customer quotes, stage defaults, and unresolved questions to align Console & Dedicated requirements.
Draft metric queries and evaluation logic (pseudo-SQL/PromQL-like) for gates: error rate, latency, GPU utilization, OOM, and queue depth; includes alternatives and caveats.
Dashboard wireframe (text form): panels per stage, breakdown by region/pool, and how to annotate promotions/rollbacks.
Brainstormed failure modes + mitigations: partial promotion, stuck gate due to missing metrics, fleet impairment mid-stage, and overload behavior.
Console UX notes: stage timeline component, promotion confirmation UX, “hold” semantics, and how to present gate evidence to customers.
Launch checklist: feature flags, migrations, backfill, canary plan, comms plan, and rollback plan for GA.
PM ticket to drive PRD completion, launch milestones, beta customer selection, and cross-functional sign-offs (SRE/Infra/Security).
PM ticket to align default gate thresholds by tier/region and decide what is configurable vs fixed for v1.
Engineering ticket: implement rollout plan CRUD + promote/abort endpoints, validation rules, persistence schema, and audit hooks.
Engineering ticket: integrate gate evaluation into policy engine; deterministic evaluation, caching, and failure-handling semantics.
Engineering ticket: implement stage-based traffic splitting / partition routing for Dedicated pools; includes multi-region considerations.
Engineering ticket: emit stage-tagged metrics/traces, manage cardinality, and ensure dashboards can attribute signals per stage.
Engineering ticket: Console backend endpoints for rollout timeline, gate evidence retrieval, and promotion/abort actions with RBAC checks.
Engineering ticket: QA automation for staging workflow (create plan → promote → gate fail → rollback), including flaky-signal simulations.
Engineering ticket: feature flags, gradual enablement, DB migrations/backfill strategy, and safe disable plan.
Design ticket: stage timeline component, gate status states, evidence drill-down UI, and customer-facing messaging for failures/holds.
Design ticket: Console audit view for promotions/aborts/overrides, including filters, export UX, and admin-only fields.
PR adds DB schema/data model for Dedicated rollout plans, including stage definitions, state machine fields, and migration/backfill scripts.
PR implements create/update/get/list APIs for rollout plans, validation (stage monotonicity, min headroom), and basic RBAC enforcement.
PR adds promote/abort endpoints, audit event emission, idempotency keys, and optimistic concurrency controls.
PR integrates gate evaluation into policy engine (latency/error/saturation), defines evaluation windows, and adds safe fallbacks on missing data.
PR updates routing layer to support stage-based partition selection for Dedicated pools; includes multi-region routing rules and unit tests.
PR adds stage identifiers to key metrics/traces, with cardinality controls and an allowlist of tags.
PR adds dashboards/alerts templates for staged rollouts: per-stage p95/p99, error rate, GPU saturation, and promotion annotations.
PR adds Console backend endpoints for rendering stage timeline, gate evidence, and action availability (promote/abort/hold).
PR introduces emergency overrides (force-promote/hold) gated by admin permissions; adds explicit audit logging and warnings in API responses.
PR adds end-to-end integration tests for staged rollouts using a simulated Dedicated pool; includes gate failure scenarios and rollback validation.
Hotfix PR reduces metrics cardinality after stage-tagging rollout (limits label set, sampling changes) and updates dashboards accordingly.
PR adds internal docs links and inline operator guidance in admin tooling; references Confluence runbook and gate thresholds.

Ticket capturing an early beta issue where stage partitioning reduced effective capacity; investigation notes link to routing PR and capacity guidelines.

Internal ticket: audit export pipeline missing new rollout event types; includes compliance impact and patch tracking.
Technical deep dive transcript with a Dedicated prospect/customer focusing on staged rollouts, gates, rollback semantics, and how Dedicated pool partitioning works.
Security review call transcript covering audit events for rollout actions, RBAC, retention, and evidence needed for enterprise approval.
